045/**
046 * RegionStates contains a set of Maps that describes the in-memory state of the AM, with the
047 * regions available in the system, the region in transition, the offline regions and the servers
048 * holding regions.
049 */
050@InterfaceAudience.Private
051public class RegionStates {
052  private static final Logger LOG = LoggerFactory.getLogger(RegionStates.class);
053
054  private final Object regionsMapLock = new Object();
055
056  private final AtomicInteger activeTransitProcedureCount = new AtomicInteger(0);
057
058  // TODO: Replace the ConcurrentSkipListMaps
059  /**
060   * A Map from {@link RegionInfo#getRegionName()} to {@link RegionStateNode}
061   */
062  private final ConcurrentSkipListMap<byte[], RegionStateNode> regionsMap =
063    new ConcurrentSkipListMap<>(Bytes.BYTES_COMPARATOR);
064
065  /**
066   * this map is a hack to lookup of region in master by encoded region name is O(n). must put and
067   * remove with regionsMap.
068   */
069  private final ConcurrentSkipListMap<String, RegionStateNode> encodedRegionsMap =
070    new ConcurrentSkipListMap<>();
071
072  /**
073   * Regions marked as offline on a read of hbase:meta. Unused or at least, once offlined, regions
074   * have no means of coming on line again. TODO.
075   */
076  private final ConcurrentSkipListMap<RegionInfo, RegionStateNode> regionOffline =
077    new ConcurrentSkipListMap<RegionInfo, RegionStateNode>();
078
079  private final ConcurrentSkipListMap<byte[], RegionFailedOpen> regionFailedOpen =
080    new ConcurrentSkipListMap<byte[], RegionFailedOpen>(Bytes.BYTES_COMPARATOR);
081
082  private final ConcurrentHashMap<ServerName, ServerStateNode> serverMap =
083    new ConcurrentHashMap<ServerName, ServerStateNode>();

086  }

093    encodedRegionsMap.clear();
094    regionOffline.clear();
095    serverMap.clear();

099  // RegionStateNode helpers

101  RegionStateNode createRegionStateNode(RegionInfo regionInfo) {
102    synchronized (regionsMapLock) {
103      RegionStateNode node = regionsMap.computeIfAbsent(regionInfo.getRegionName(),
104        key -> new RegionStateNode(regionInfo, activeTransitProcedureCount));
105
106      if (encodedRegionsMap.get(regionInfo.getEncodedName()) != node) {
107        encodedRegionsMap.put(regionInfo.getEncodedName(), node);
108      }
109
110      return node;
111    }
112  }
113
114  public RegionStateNode getOrCreateRegionStateNode(RegionInfo regionInfo) {
115    RegionStateNode node = getRegionStateNodeFromName(regionInfo.getRegionName());
116    return node != null ? node : createRegionStateNode(regionInfo);
117  }
118
119  public RegionStateNode getRegionStateNodeFromName(byte[] regionName) {
120    return regionsMap.get(regionName);
121  }
122
123  public RegionStateNode getRegionStateNodeFromEncodedRegionName(final String encodedRegionName) {
124    return encodedRegionsMap.get(encodedRegionName);
125  }
126
127  public RegionStateNode getRegionStateNode(RegionInfo regionInfo) {
128    return getRegionStateNodeFromName(regionInfo.getRegionName());
129  }
130
131  public void deleteRegion(final RegionInfo regionInfo) {
132    synchronized (regionsMapLock) {
133      regionsMap.remove(regionInfo.getRegionName());
134      encodedRegionsMap.remove(regionInfo.getEncodedName());
135    }
136    // Remove from the offline regions map too if there.
137    if (this.regionOffline.containsKey(regionInfo)) {
138      if (LOG.isTraceEnabled()) LOG.trace("Removing from regionOffline Map: " + regionInfo);
139      this.regionOffline.remove(regionInfo);
140    }
141  }
142
143  public void deleteRegions(final List<RegionInfo> regionInfos) {
144    regionInfos.forEach(this::deleteRegion);
145  }

147  List<RegionStateNode> getTableRegionStateNodes(final TableName tableName) {
148    final ArrayList<RegionStateNode> regions = new ArrayList<RegionStateNode>();
149    for (RegionStateNode node : regionsMap.tailMap(tableName.getName()).values()) {
150      if (!node.getTable().equals(tableName)) break;
151      regions.add(node);
152    }
153    return regions;
154  }
155
156  ArrayList<RegionState> getTableRegionStates(final TableName tableName) {
157    final ArrayList<RegionState> regions = new ArrayList<RegionState>();
158    for (RegionStateNode node : regionsMap.tailMap(tableName.getName()).values()) {
159      if (!node.getTable().equals(tableName)) break;
160      regions.add(node.toRegionState());
161    }
162    return regions;
163  }

165  ArrayList<RegionInfo> getTableRegionsInfo(final TableName tableName) {
166    final ArrayList<RegionInfo> regions = new ArrayList<RegionInfo>();
167    for (RegionStateNode node : regionsMap.tailMap(tableName.getName()).values()) {
168      if (!node.getTable().equals(tableName)) break;
169      regions.add(node.getRegionInfo());
170    }
171    return regions;
172  }

218  private HRegionLocation createRegionForReopen(RegionStateNode node) {
219    node.lock();
220    try {
221      if (!include(node, false)) {
222        return null;
223      }
224      if (node.isInState(State.OPEN)) {
225        return new HRegionLocation(node.getRegionInfo(), node.getRegionLocation(),
226          node.getOpenSeqNum());
227      } else if (node.isInState(State.OPENING)) {
228        return new HRegionLocation(node.getRegionInfo(), node.getRegionLocation(), -1);
229      } else {
230        return null;
231      }
232    } finally {
233      node.unlock();
234    }
235  }
236
237  /**
238   * Get the regions to be reopened when modifying a table.
239   * <p/>
240   * Notice that the {@code openSeqNum} in the returned HRegionLocation is also used to indicate the
241   * state of this region, positive means the region is in {@link State#OPEN}, -1 means
242   * {@link State#OPENING}. And for regions in other states we do not need reopen them.
243   */
244  public List<HRegionLocation> getRegionsOfTableForReopen(TableName tableName) {
245    return getTableRegionStateNodes(tableName).stream().map(this::createRegionForReopen)
246      .filter(r -> r != null).collect(Collectors.toList());
247  }
248
249  /**
250   * Check whether the region has been reopened. The meaning of the {@link HRegionLocation} is the
251   * same with {@link #getRegionsOfTableForReopen(TableName)}.
252   * <p/>
253   * For a region which is in {@link State#OPEN} before, if the region state is changed or the open
254   * seq num is changed, we can confirm that it has been reopened.
255   * <p/>
256   * For a region which is in {@link State#OPENING} before, usually it will be in {@link State#OPEN}
257   * now and we will schedule a MRP to reopen it. But there are several exceptions:
258   * <ul>
259   * <li>The region is in state other than {@link State#OPEN} or {@link State#OPENING}.</li>
260   * <li>The location of the region has been changed</li>
261   * </ul>
262   * Of course the region could still be in {@link State#OPENING} state and still on the same
263   * server, then here we will still return a {@link HRegionLocation} for it, just like
264   * {@link #getRegionsOfTableForReopen(TableName)}.
265   * @param oldLoc the previous state/location of this region
266   * @return null if the region has been reopened, otherwise a new {@link HRegionLocation} which
267   *         means we still need to reopen the region.
268   * @see #getRegionsOfTableForReopen(TableName)
269   */
270  public HRegionLocation checkReopened(HRegionLocation oldLoc) {
271    RegionStateNode node = getRegionStateNode(oldLoc.getRegion());
272    // HBASE-20921
273    // if the oldLoc's state node does not exist, that means the region is
274    // merged or split, no need to check it
275    if (node == null) {
276      return null;
277    }
278    node.lock();
279    try {
280      if (oldLoc.getSeqNum() >= 0) {
281        // in OPEN state before
282        if (node.isInState(State.OPEN)) {
283          if (node.getOpenSeqNum() > oldLoc.getSeqNum()) {
284            // normal case, the region has been reopened
285            return null;
286          } else {
287            // the open seq num does not change, need to reopen again
288            return new HRegionLocation(node.getRegionInfo(), node.getRegionLocation(),
289              node.getOpenSeqNum());
290          }
291        } else {
292          // the state has been changed so we can make sure that the region has been reopened(not
293          // finished maybe, but not a problem).
294          return null;
295        }
296      } else {
297        // in OPENING state before
298        if (!node.isInState(State.OPEN, State.OPENING)) {
299          // not in OPEN or OPENING state, then we can make sure that the region has been
300          // reopened(not finished maybe, but not a problem)
301          return null;
302        } else {
303          if (!node.getRegionLocation().equals(oldLoc.getServerName())) {
304            // the region has been moved, so we can make sure that the region has been reopened.
305            return null;
306          }
307          // normal case, we are still in OPENING state, or the reopen has been opened and the state
308          // is changed to OPEN.
309          long openSeqNum = node.isInState(State.OPEN) ? node.getOpenSeqNum() : -1;
310          return new HRegionLocation(node.getRegionInfo(), node.getRegionLocation(), openSeqNum);
311        }
312      }
313    } finally {
314      node.unlock();
315    }
316  }

318  /**
319   * Get the regions for enabling a table.
320   * <p/>
321   * Here we want the EnableTableProcedure to be more robust and can be used to fix some nasty
322   * states, so the checks in this method will be a bit strange. In general, a region can only be
323   * offline when it is split, for merging we will just delete the parent regions, but with HBCK we
324   * may force update the state of a region to fix some nasty bugs, so in this method we will try to
325   * bring the offline regions back if it is not split. That's why we only check for split state
326   * here.
327   */
328  public List<RegionInfo> getRegionsOfTableForEnabling(TableName table) {
329    return getRegionsOfTable(table,
330      regionNode -> !regionNode.isInState(State.SPLIT) && !regionNode.getRegionInfo().isSplit());
331  }

333  /**
334   * Returns all regions of the table, irrespective of assignment or split/offline state.
335   */
336  public List<RegionInfo> getAllRegionsOfTable(TableName table) {
337    return getTableRegionStateNodes(table).stream().map(RegionStateNode::getRegionInfo)
338      .collect(Collectors.toList());
339  }

341  /**
342   * Get the regions for deleting a table.
343   * <p/>
344   * Here we need to return all the regions irrespective of the states in order to archive them all.
345   * This is because if we don't archive OFFLINE/SPLIT regions and if a snapshot or a cloned table
346   * references to the regions, we will lose the data of the regions.
347   */
348  public List<RegionInfo> getRegionsOfTableForDeleting(TableName table) {
349    return getAllRegionsOfTable(table);
350  }

352  /** Returns Return the regions of the table and filter them. */
353  private List<RegionInfo> getRegionsOfTable(TableName table, Predicate<RegionStateNode> filter) {
354    return getTableRegionStateNodes(table).stream().filter(filter).map(n -> n.getRegionInfo())
355      .collect(Collectors.toList());
356  }

358  /**
359   * Utility. Whether to include region in list of regions. Default is to weed out split and offline
360   * regions.
361   * @return True if we should include the <code>node</code> (do not include if split or offline
362   *         unless <code>offline</code> is set to true.
363   */
364  private boolean include(final RegionStateNode node, final boolean offline) {
365    if (LOG.isTraceEnabled()) {
366      LOG.trace("WORKING ON " + node + " " + node.getRegionInfo());
367    }
368    final RegionInfo hri = node.getRegionInfo();
369    if (node.isInState(State.SPLIT) || hri.isSplit()) {
370      return false;
371    }
372    if ((node.isInState(State.OFFLINE) || hri.isOffline()) && !offline) {
373      return false;
374    }
375    return (!hri.isOffline() && !hri.isSplit()) || ((hri.isOffline() || hri.isSplit()) && offline);
376  }

423  public void updateRegionState(RegionInfo regionInfo, State state) {
424    RegionStateNode regionNode = getOrCreateRegionStateNode(regionInfo);
425    regionNode.lock();
426    try {
427      regionNode.setState(state);
428    } finally {
429      regionNode.unlock();
430    }
431  }

446  public boolean isRegionInState(RegionInfo regionInfo, State... state) {
447    RegionStateNode regionNode = getRegionStateNode(regionInfo);
448    if (regionNode != null) {
449      regionNode.lock();
450      try {
451        return regionNode.isInState(state);
452      } finally {
453        regionNode.unlock();

468  public Map<ServerName, List<RegionInfo>>
469    getSnapShotOfAssignment(final Collection<RegionInfo> regions) {
470    final Map<ServerName, List<RegionInfo>> result = new HashMap<ServerName, List<RegionInfo>>();
471    if (regions != null) {
472      for (RegionInfo hri : regions) {
473        final RegionStateNode node = getRegionStateNode(hri);
474        if (node == null) {
475          continue;
476        }
477        createSnapshot(node, result);
478      }
479    } else {
480      for (RegionStateNode node : regionsMap.values()) {
481        if (node == null) {
482          continue;
483        }
484        createSnapshot(node, result);
485      }
486    }
487    return result;
488  }
489
490  private void createSnapshot(RegionStateNode node, Map<ServerName, List<RegionInfo>> result) {
491    final ServerName serverName = node.getRegionLocation();
492    if (serverName == null) {
493      return;
494    }
495
496    List<RegionInfo> serverRegions = result.get(serverName);
497    if (serverRegions == null) {
498      serverRegions = new ArrayList<RegionInfo>();
499      result.put(serverName, serverRegions);
500    }
501    serverRegions.add(node.getRegionInfo());
502  }

504  public Map<RegionInfo, ServerName> getRegionAssignments() {
505    final HashMap<RegionInfo, ServerName> assignments = new HashMap<RegionInfo, ServerName>();
506    for (RegionStateNode node : regionsMap.values()) {
507      assignments.put(node.getRegionInfo(), node.getRegionLocation());
508    }
509    return assignments;
510  }

512  public Map<RegionState.State, List<RegionInfo>> getRegionByStateOfTable(TableName tableName) {
513    final State[] states = State.values();
514    final Map<RegionState.State, List<RegionInfo>> tableRegions =
515      new HashMap<State, List<RegionInfo>>(states.length);
516    for (int i = 0; i < states.length; ++i) {
517      tableRegions.put(states[i], new ArrayList<RegionInfo>());
518    }
519
520    for (RegionStateNode node : regionsMap.values()) {
521      if (node.getTable().equals(tableName)) {
522        tableRegions.get(node.getState()).add(node.getRegionInfo());
523      }
524    }
525    return tableRegions;
526  }

528  public ServerName getRegionServerOfRegion(RegionInfo regionInfo) {
529    RegionStateNode regionNode = getRegionStateNode(regionInfo);
530    if (regionNode != null) {
531      regionNode.lock();
532      try {
533        ServerName server = regionNode.getRegionLocation();
534        return server != null ? server : regionNode.getLastHost();
535      } finally {
536        regionNode.unlock();
537      }
538    }
539    return null;
540  }
541
542  /**
543   * This is an EXPENSIVE clone. Cloning though is the safest thing to do. Can't let out original
544   * since it can change and at least the load balancer wants to iterate this exported list. We need
545   * to synchronize on regions since all access to this.servers is under a lock on this.regions.
546   * @return A clone of current open or opening assignments.
547   */
548  public Map<TableName, Map<ServerName, List<RegionInfo>>>
549    getAssignmentsForBalancer(TableStateManager tableStateManager, List<ServerName> onlineServers) {
550    final Map<TableName, Map<ServerName, List<RegionInfo>>> result = new HashMap<>();
551    for (RegionStateNode node : regionsMap.values()) {
552      // DisableTableProcedure first sets the table state to DISABLED and then force unassigns
553      // the regions in a loop. The balancer should ignore all regions for tables in DISABLED
554      // state because even if still currently open we expect them to be offlined very soon.
555      if (isTableDisabled(tableStateManager, node.getTable())) {
556        if (LOG.isTraceEnabled()) {
557          LOG.trace("Ignoring {} because table is disabled", node);
558        }
559        continue;
560      }
561      // When balancing, we are only interested in OPEN or OPENING regions. These can be
562      // expected to remain online until the next balancer iteration or unless the balancer
563      // decides to move it. Regions in other states are not eligible for balancing, because
564      // they are closing, splitting, merging, or otherwise already in transition.
565      if (!node.isInState(State.OPEN, State.OPENING)) {
566        if (LOG.isTraceEnabled()) {
567          LOG.trace("Ignoring {} because region is not OPEN or OPENING", node);
568        }
569        continue;
570      }
571      Map<ServerName, List<RegionInfo>> tableResult =
572        result.computeIfAbsent(node.getTable(), t -> new HashMap<>());
573      final ServerName serverName = node.getRegionLocation();
574      // A region in ONLINE or OPENING state should have a location.
575      if (serverName == null) {
576        LOG.warn("Skipping, no server for {}", node);
577        continue;
578      }
579      List<RegionInfo> serverResult =
580        tableResult.computeIfAbsent(serverName, s -> new ArrayList<>());
581      serverResult.add(node.getRegionInfo());
582    }
583    // Add online servers with no assignment for the table.
584    for (Map<ServerName, List<RegionInfo>> table : result.values()) {
585      for (ServerName serverName : onlineServers) {
586        table.computeIfAbsent(serverName, key -> new ArrayList<>());
587      }
588    }
589    return result;
590  }
591
592  private boolean isTableDisabled(final TableStateManager tableStateManager,
593    final TableName tableName) {
594    return tableStateManager.isTableState(tableName, TableState.State.DISABLED,
595      TableState.State.DISABLING);
596  }

614  public static final class RegionFailedOpen {
615    private final RegionStateNode regionNode;
616
617    private volatile Exception exception = null;
618    private AtomicInteger retries = new AtomicInteger();
619
620    public RegionFailedOpen(final RegionStateNode regionNode) {
621      this.regionNode = regionNode;
622    }
623
624    public RegionStateNode getRegionStateNode() {
625      return regionNode;
626    }
627
628    public RegionInfo getRegionInfo() {
629      return regionNode.getRegionInfo();
630    }
631
632    public int incrementAndGetRetries() {
633      return this.retries.incrementAndGet();
634    }
635
636    public int getRetries() {
637      return retries.get();
638    }
639
640    public void setException(final Exception exception) {
641      this.exception = exception;
642    }
643
644    public Exception getException() {
645      return this.exception;
646    }
647  }
648
649  public RegionFailedOpen addToFailedOpen(final RegionStateNode regionNode) {
650    final byte[] key = regionNode.getRegionInfo().getRegionName();
651    return regionFailedOpen.computeIfAbsent(key, (k) -> new RegionFailedOpen(regionNode));
652  }
653
654  public RegionFailedOpen getFailedOpen(final RegionInfo regionInfo) {
655    return regionFailedOpen.get(regionInfo.getRegionName());
656  }
657
658  public void removeFromFailedOpen(final RegionInfo regionInfo) {
659    regionFailedOpen.remove(regionInfo.getRegionName());
660  }
661
662  public List<RegionState> getRegionFailedOpen() {
663    if (regionFailedOpen.isEmpty()) return Collections.emptyList();
664
665    ArrayList<RegionState> regions = new ArrayList<RegionState>(regionFailedOpen.size());
666    for (RegionFailedOpen r : regionFailedOpen.values()) {
667      regions.add(r.getRegionStateNode().toRegionState());
668    }
669    return regions;
670  }
671
672  // ==========================================================================
673  // Servers
674  // ==========================================================================
675
676  /**
677   * Create the ServerStateNode when registering a new region server
678   */
679  public void createServer(ServerName serverName) {
680    serverMap.computeIfAbsent(serverName, key -> new ServerStateNode(key));
681  }
682
683  /**
684   * Called by SCP at end of successful processing.
685   */
686  public void removeServer(ServerName serverName) {
687    serverMap.remove(serverName);
688  }
689
690  /** Returns Pertinent ServerStateNode or NULL if none found (Do not make modifications). */
691  public ServerStateNode getServerNode(final ServerName serverName) {
692    return serverMap.get(serverName);
693  }
694
695  public double getAverageLoad() {
696    int numServers = 0;
697    int totalLoad = 0;
698    for (ServerStateNode node : serverMap.values()) {
699      totalLoad += node.getRegionCount();
700      numServers++;
701    }
702    return numServers == 0 ? 0.0 : (double) totalLoad / (double) numServers;
703  }
704
705  public void addRegionToServer(final RegionStateNode regionNode) {
706    ServerStateNode serverNode = getServerNode(regionNode.getRegionLocation());
707    serverNode.addRegion(regionNode);
708  }
709
710  public void removeRegionFromServer(final ServerName serverName,
711    final RegionStateNode regionNode) {
712    ServerStateNode serverNode = getServerNode(serverName);
713    // here the server node could be null. For example, if there is already a TRSP for a region and
714    // at the same time, the target server is crashed and there is a SCP. The SCP will interrupt the
715    // TRSP and the TRSP will first set the region as abnormally closed and remove it from the
716    // server node. But here, this TRSP is not a child procedure of the SCP, so it is possible that
717    // the SCP finishes, thus removes the server node for this region server, before the TRSP wakes
718    // up and enter here to remove the region node from the server node, then we will get a null
719    // server node here.
720    if (serverNode != null) {
721      serverNode.removeRegion(regionNode);
722    }
723  }

725  // ==========================================================================
726  // ToString helpers
727  // ==========================================================================
728  public static String regionNamesToString(final Collection<byte[]> regions) {
729    final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
730    final Iterator<byte[]> it = regions.iterator();
731    sb.append("[");
732    if (it.hasNext()) {
733      sb.append(Bytes.toStringBinary(it.next()));
734      while (it.hasNext()) {
735        sb.append(", ");
736        sb.append(Bytes.toStringBinary(it.next()));
737      }
738    }
739    sb.append("]");
740    return sb.toString();
741  }
742}
